concept.title: How you know it works
concept.shortdesc: holds out TPU7x. It drafts the TPU7x topics from the v5p and v6e topics and the TPU7x values, and then compares each draft with the page that Google published. Six measured values decide whether the MVP works.

conbody.p: The table at the top of the page shows each target beside the value the latest runs measured. Every value comes from a check result or a run record, not from a judgment.

row.entry: Drafts that reach a writer and fail the DITA grammar
Every logged run counts the topics it emitted that fail the OASIS DITA RELAX NG grammar. A topic that fails is withheld, so it never reaches a writer.
Values with a key or a source

The grounding check counts every value in the drafts: key references, table cells and any number typed into prose. A value counts as sourced when it is a key, or when it matches a fact with the same unit.
Edit ratio on topics that have a sibling
The share of tokens a writer must change to turn the draft into the published TPU7x topic. See .
Time from issue to draft pull requests for the set
From the time the issue is opened to the time the last draft pull request opens, from the latest Git-path run record.
Open draft comments in the drafts when a pull request merges, from the merge record. The alignr/open-questions status blocks a merge while any is open.
Runs whose record holds model calls, tokens and cost.

conbody.p: A status of Pending means that nothing has measured the value yet, for example no draft pull request has merged.

section.title: Known limits
section.p: drafts what has a sibling. A concept that's new in a generation, such as the TPU7x dual-chiplet design, gets a stub with questions instead of prose. lxml checks the grammar but doesn't apply the default attribute values that DITA processing needs, so DITA-OT still builds every topic in CI.
